about: Lines Krish read and rejected, in his words. Every script is checked against them (scripts/post-pack/story_check.py): a pattern here is refused in any future script, so the same mistake is never made twice. Add each new rejection the moment he gives it, with his words.

rejected.instead: say encrypted, and what it means, once
rejected.said: "Or a locked box that even the company can't open" needs so much interpretation to understand

rejected.instead: say who pays and for what: shops paying to be the one it recommends
rejected.said: "Of course Meta will sell what its helper picks." makes no sense either

rejected.pattern: \bwrote to a shop that overcharged someone\b
rejected.instead: open on the thing itself, then the example
rejected.said: "Meta's new AI helper, Muse, wrote to a shop that overcharged someone by thousands of dollars." is such a weird opening line

rejected.instead: say the idea the way he'd say it to a friend
rejected.said: these video scripts are still waffle, they dont sound like me and I cant read them coherently

rejected.instead: name it every time: Meta, OpenAI, Google, Apple
rejected.said: its still not clear enough it doesn't introduce why Muse is different to just using Claude. "It can live in three places on your phone and on the company's servers, where the company can get to it." etc is so confusing, it makes no sense when read out. Who is "the company"? What is "It"?
